name: Srinagar
description: Srinagar is the summer capital of Jammu & Kashmir, set at around 1,600 metres in the Kashmir Valley on the banks of Dal Lake. It suits travellers drawn to Mughal gardens, Sufi shrines, shikara rides, and the famed houseboats of Dal and Nagin lakes, though the security situation and political sensitivity should factor into trip planning. The city rewards those who linger — a rushed two-day pass misses most of it.
nearest_railhead: Banihal (Udhampur–Baramulla Rail Link; Srinagar station under development as of 2025 — most visitors arrive by rail to Udhampur/Jammu Tawi then road/air)
nearest_airport: Sheikh ul-Alam International Airport (SXR), Srinagar — approximately 15 km from Dal Lake

attractions.name: Dal Lake
attractions.description: The iconic glacial lake that defines Srinagar, best experienced by shikara at dawn when the mist sits low and vegetable sellers pole their boats to the floating market. Houseboats line the eastern shore and range from dilapidated to genuinely grand; quality varies enormously so inspect before booking.

attractions.name: Shalimar Bagh
attractions.description: The largest of Srinagar's Mughal gardens, laid out by Emperor Jahangir in 1619 for Empress Nur Jahan, with four terraced chenar-lined channels rising toward the Zabarwan hills. Most striking in April when the tulips and cherries bloom, or in autumn when the chinars turn gold.

attractions.name: Nishat Bagh
attractions.description: The second major Mughal garden on Dal Lake's eastern shore, built by Nur Jahan's brother Asif Khan in 1632, with twelve terraces representing the signs of the zodiac and sweeping views across the lake to the Pir Panjal range. Gets crowded on weekends; go on a weekday morning.

attractions.name: Hazratbal Shrine
attractions.description: The most revered Muslim shrine in Kashmir, on the western shore of Dal Lake, said to house a hair relic of the Prophet Muhammad. The white marble dome is architecturally graceful and the Friday congregation is one of the largest gatherings in the valley; visitors should dress conservatively and be respectful of prayers.

attractions.name: Shankaracharya Temple
attractions.description: A Shiva temple perched at 1,100 feet on the Shankaracharya Hill, reached by a staircase of roughly 250 steps from the road; the climb is moderate but exposed and not suitable for those with mobility issues. The panoramic view over Dal Lake, the old city, and the ring of mountains is among the best in Srinagar.

attractions.name: Jama Masjid
attractions.description: Built in 1394 by Sultan Sikandar and later expanded, this is the principal congregational mosque of Srinagar, notable for its 378 wooden pillars each fashioned from a single deodar trunk and its Indo-Saracenic courtyard. It sits in the heart of the old city and is surrounded by bazaars selling shawls, spices, and dried fruit.

attractions.name: Old City Bazaars (Nowhatta, Zaina Kadal, Maharaj Gunj)
attractions.description: The old city's interlocking bazaars are the best place to buy Kashmiri handicrafts at non-tourist prices — papier-mâché, walnut-wood carving, pashmina, and sozni embroidery. The lanes around Nowhatta and Zaina Kadal retain genuine 19th-century wooden architecture with carved balconies; most is slowly disappearing so it is worth seeing now.

attractions.name: Gulmarg (Meadow of Flowers)
attractions.description: At around 2,650 metres, Gulmarg is a large alpine meadow roughly 56 km from Srinagar, famous for skiing in winter (December–February) and the Gondola cable car that reaches 3,980 metres for views of Nanga Parbat. The meadow walk in summer is straightforward, but Phase 2 of the gondola to Kongdori–Apharwat involves cold, altitude, and some scrambling.

attractions.name: Pahalgam & Betaab Valley
attractions.description: Pahalgam is a hill resort at 2,130 metres on the Lidder River, 95 km from Srinagar, and serves as the staging point for the Amarnath Yatra pilgrimage. Betaab Valley, a few kilometres further, is a wide open glacial meadow named after a 1983 Bollywood film and is the most accessible taste of high Kashmir meadow scenery without serious trekking.

attractions.name: Nagin Lake (Hidden Gem)
attractions.description: Separated from Dal by a narrow causeway, Nagin is smaller, quieter, and considerably less commercial — most of the floating gardens and lotus beds here see only local fishermen. A shikara on Nagin at dusk is one of the more genuinely peaceful experiences left in the Srinagar basin, and houseboat prices are noticeably lower.

attractions.name: Dachigam National Park (Hidden Gem)
attractions.description: A 141 sq km protected area just 22 km from Srinagar, and the last stronghold of the critically endangered Hangul (Kashmir stag). Entry requires a permit from the J&K Wildlife Department and visits are restricted to a guide-accompanied zone; sightings are not guaranteed but the riparian forest and bird life alone repay the effort for wildlife enthusiasts.
